explanation.text: The Emancipation Proclamation applied only to states in rebellion on January 1, 1863, excluding areas under Union control.
New Orleans and surrounding parishes in Louisiana were explicitly exempted from the Emancipation Proclamation because they were under Union control and regarded as loyal.
The Final Emancipation Proclamation did not cover the city of New Orleans, as it was among the areas exempted due to Union occupation.

excerpts.text: The Emancipation Proclamation applied only in the ten states that were still in rebellion on January 1, 1863, namely South Carolina, Mississippi, Florida, Alabama, Georgia, Louisiana, Texas, Virginia, Arkansas, North Carolina.

Specific exemptions were stated for other areas under Union control on January 1, 1863, namely 48 counties that would soon become [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia "West Virginia"), seven other named counties of [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia") including Berkeley county, which was soon added to West Virginia, [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans") and 13 named parishes nearby.[[27]](#cite_note-28)

Martin, and Orleans, including the city of New Orleans), [Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi "Mississippi"), [Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama "Alabama"), [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida"), [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)"), [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina "South Carolina"), [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina"), and [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia") (except the forty-eight counties designated as West Virginia, and also the counties of Berkley, Accomac, Northampton, Elizabeth City, York, Princess Ann, and Norfolk, including the cities of Norfolk and Portsmouth)."[[b]](#cite_note-30)[[29]](#cite_note-31)[[30]](#cite_note-:6-32)

Also, six additional counties and two independent cities[[c]](#cite_note-33) were exempted in the Union-controlled [Tidewater region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidewater_(region) "Tidewater (region)") of [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia").[[31]](#cite_note-34) And, in [Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana "Louisiana"), the city of [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans")[[d]](#cite_note-35) and the 13 named parishes were exempted because Lincoln regarded them as loyal to the Union.

excerpts.text: It designated the areas considered to still be in rebellion, but also those under Union control and thus exempted from the proclamation. The exempted areas included parishes in Louisiana and the city of New Orleans, several cities and counties in Virginia, and all of the counties in what would become the new state of West Virginia. Slaves living in those Union-occupied exempted areas were considered outside of the president's war powers, and would remain enslaved after January 1.
